title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Stadtwerke Frankenthal GmbH: Vergabe von Leistungen der Objektplanung für Ingenieurbauwerke für die Errichtung eines Wärmenetzes in Frankenthal (Los 1)
description: Die Stadtwerke Frankenthal GmbH ist ein kommunales Energieversorgungsunternehmen mit Sitz in Frankenthal (Pfalz). Sie versorgt die Stadt Frankenthal sowie angrenzende Gemeinden im Rhein-Pfalz-Kreis. Der derzeitige Versorgungsschwerpunkt liegt auf der Gasversorgung. Im Zuge der Energiewende soll diese schrittweise durch ein modernes Fernwärmenetz ersetzt werden. Im Rahmen der Bundesförderung für effiziente Wärmenetze, Modul 1, wurde hierfür eine Machbarkeitsstudie erstellt. Auf Grundlage dieser Studie wurde das östliche Stadtgebiet als erstes Ausbaugebiet von insgesamt zwei Ausbaugebieten zum Wärmenetzausbau festgelegt. Das erste Ausbaugebiet umschließt den Wärmenetzausbau bis 2032 und das zweite Ausbaugebiet umschließt den Wärmenetzausbau bis 2045. Das zweite Ausbaugebiet dient ausschließlich als langfristiger Ziel- und Betrachtungsraum für den Netzausbau bis 2045. Die konkrete Umsetzung ist nicht Gegenstand der ausgeschriebenen Planungsleistungen und kann auf Grundlage der Planungsergebnisse in mehrere Teilgebiete und Ausbaustufen untergliedert werden. Das vorliegende Vergabeverfahren bezieht sich auf den flächendeckenden Ausbau des Wärmenetzes für das erste Ausbaugebiet. Im ersten Ausbaugebiet soll ein Wärmenetz errichtet werden, das seine Wärme aus einer vorgelagerten Wärmeerzeugung bezieht. Der Übergabepunkt zum Vorlieferanten soll hydraulisch entkoppelt und ausschließlich über einen Wärmetauscher thermisch mit der Transportleitung des Wärmevorlieferanten gekoppelt werden. Es handelt sich insgesamt um zwei Übergabepunkte bzw. -stationen die sich einmal nord- und südöstlich außerhalb der Stadtgrenzen befinden. Für das Wärmenetz ist vorgesehen, dass es im Endausbau im Zieljahr 2045 einen jährlichen Wärmeabsatz von etwa 100 GWh erreicht. Die ausgeschriebene Planungsleistung umfasst zunächst den flächendeckenden Wärmenetzausbau im östlichen Stadtgebiet bis zum Jahr 2032 (erstes Ausbaugebiet). Der angestrebte Wärmeabsatz im Endausbau soll anschließend über das zweite Ausbaugebiet bis zum Jahr 2045 erreicht werden. Die Stadtwerke Frankenthal GmbH beabsichtigen, Planungsleistungen für die Errichtung des Wärmenetzes zu vergeben. Für die zu vergebenden Planungsleistungen bis einschließlich Leistungsphase 4 HOAI wurde ein BEW-Modul 1-Förderantrag gestellt. Für die darauf aufbauenden Planungsleistungen wird voraussichtlich ein BEW-Modul 2-Förderantrag gestellt werden.

description: Der Auftraggeber erweitert seine Heizzentrale am Hartmut-Hermann-Weg 4 in 85716 Unterschleißheim. title: Dredged Material Containment Area (DMCA) O&M Construction IDC
description: Purpose: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Savannah District, is seeking information from industry to determine the availability and capability of qualified contractors is to provide general construction for the new construction, rehabilitation, replacement, repair, and construction-related maintenance of Dredged Material Containment Areas (DMCAs) and associated infrastructure within Savannah and Brunswick Harbors. All work shall be performed in a safe, timely, and cost-effective manner. This notice is issued for the purpose of conducting market research. This is not a Solicitation Announcement, nor is it a Request for Proposal. The Government is contemplating a potential acquisition strategy. The results of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The Government is seeking to identify capable firms, including small businesses, that have recent and relevant experience in performing DMCA-related construction work, such as site preparation, dike construction and repair, weir/structure rehabilitation, erosion control, grading, and general access improvements. Task orders will be executed using the Design-Bid-Build (DBB) delivery method. The Contractor will perform construction in accordance with Government-furnished designs. Requirements: Work under this contract is restricted to the designated DMCAs, bird islands, and directly associated supporting infrastructure located within the Savannah and Brunswick Harbor operational footprints: Savannah Harbor Facilities: Disposal Areas 1N, 2A, 12A, 13A, 13B, 14A, and 14B; Jones/Oysterbed Island (JOI); and associated bird islands. Brunswick Harbor Facilities: Andrews Island DMCA. The Government anticipates awarding a Firm-Fixed Price Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Construction Contract with an expected effective date in late FY27 � early FY28. The anticipated contract period of performance is five (5) years. The contract will provide for the construction, rehabilitation, replacement, repair, and construction-related maintenance of Dredged Material Containment Areas (DMCAs) and associated infrastructure within Savannah and Brunswick Harbors. All work shall be performed in a safe, timely, and cost-effective manner in accordance with the requirements of this contract and individual task orders. The Contractor shall furnish all necessary supervision, labor, materials, equipment, transportation, temporary facilities, construction quality control, and other resources required to complete construction activities under individual task orders in accordance with the applicable contract requirements. Individual task orders will establish specific work limits, requirements, and completion criteria. Task orders will be issued based on the Government�s requirements and may specify performance durations (e.g., calendar days). Representative construction and maintenance tasks may include, but are not limited to construction, rehabilitation, repair, and maintenance of designated DMCA infrastructure, including dikes, embankments, roads, access areas, drainage and water-control systems, shoreline protection, marine access features, and associated structural, mechanical, and electrical components. Supporting activities may include earthwork, excavation, material handling, dewatering, vegetation and debris removal, erosion control, site restoration, surveys, utility protection, temporary facilities, waterborne access, testing, and documentation necessary to complete authorized task orders. All work shall comply with applicable environmental, material handling, disposal, seasonal, and access requirements. General building construction and HVAC work are excluded. title: Retail Space to Lease - Delano, CA
description: The Los Angeles District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is seeking to lease a minimum of 1,381 net/usable to a maximum of 1,874 gross/rentable square feet (gross square feet to include any common area factor), of existing Class A or B retail space, in Delano, CA, within the defined Delineated area (DA) boundaries below: North -- South -- East � West � The Government�s desire is for a full-service lease of Retail space for an Armed Forces Career Center for a term not to exceed five (5) years with Government termination rights. Offered space must meet Government requirements per the terms of the Government Lease. Interested respondents may include building owners and representatives with the exclusive right to represent building owners. Representatives of building owners must include the exclusivity agreement, representation letter, listing contract or other executed agreement granting the exclusive right to represent the building owner with their response to this advertisement. Adequate mass transit (buses, trains, rail cars) for the public within three walking blocks is highly desired. REQUIRED Spaces MUST offer both a primary and a secondary point of ingress/egress. Lighted, non-exclusive or reserved on-site parking for four 5 marked government owned vehicles must be provided for on 24 hours 7 days a week basis. Additional lighted parking must be available during business hours, weekends and holidays, for approximately 5 employee vehicles and visitors/recruit candidate parking. Must use the Government Lease. The military services shall have the right to use space beyond normal working hours and, if required, on Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays. This includes the use of elevators, lights, toilet facilities, and, if necessary, heating and air conditioning. Armed Forces Recruiting Facilities are only located in defined geographical areas that contain businesses and other establishments that are of a compatible nature. Under no circumstances will be these facilities to be in areas where sexually oriented businesses, bars, nightclubs, liquor stores, smoke shops, marijuana dispensaries etc. or other business that produce injurious odors detectable with the leased spaces. Placement near these establishments can hamper overall production of the office or cause concern for the safety of the personnel stationed there and their visitors. Lessors are required to be registered and active in www.sam.gov prior to the deadline for final offer submission. Proposals are due no later than 5:00 pm (PST) on November 27, 2026. Responses should include: Building name and address As-built floor plan drawing Digital photo of street view of property Area (BOMA rentable square feet & BOMA usable square feet) Rental rate per square foot rentable space to include (CAM, Taxes and insurance) Common area factor(s) for available space, if applicable Following are the factors that will be considered when evaluating bids/offers: 1. Location 2. Ability to meet all construction specifications, security measures and lease requirements 3. Complete initial and final offers must be received by defined deadline 4. Competitive costs in the best interest of the government 5. Qualitative ratings by client for mission Additional Notes: Three (3) construction bids for the build-out are requested. After a bid is accepted, no change orders are authorized, so bids need to be accurate and complete (including all taxes and fees). Special attention should be given to security requirements (video entry control system, closed circuit television system and video recording, dual roller shades on exterior windows, fixed panel shade on exterior entry door and peep hole in secondary exit, perforated window wrap), fragmentation film on exterior windows/glass doors, telecommunication wiring requirements, addition of water fountain, signage, paint, wall graphics, phone jacks, electrical outlets, and spec'd carpet squares. These are items that can add a significant cost and may be overlooked in the bid process; however, all items in the specifications need to be followed, even if code does not require the item (i.e., smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, etc.). Bids shall include any tear down/haul away expenses. The attached floor plan is to be used as a generalized idea and reference tool for proximity of amount of useable space this location will require for build out in both office space and common area space. Submitted floor plans must meet the space requirements as designated on attached example. It is mandatory that janitorial services be included in the lease (lessor responsible for contracting these services). Be sure to review the attached janitorial guidance and ensure the costs of these services are included on the rental proposal works CONTACT Interested parties may contact Almer Capalac at the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Los Angeles Branch, Real Estate Office, (213) 431-5290; almer.capalac@usace.army.mil, no later than 5:00 PM MST on November 27, 2026.

description: The objective of this action is to strengthen transatlantic collaboration to promote EU interests and priorities in important policy areas, demonstrate the EU's global reach, address global challenges and amplify shared values. Public diplomacy and policy support are relevant tools contributing to improved transatlantic relations: maintaining the EU-US partnership requires actively engaging key stakeholders and audiences to fundamentally raise awareness of the EU, amplify our shared values, and promote the importance of the EU-US relationship among them. On the one hand, the action will enhance EU foreign policy objectives through strategic public diplomacy activities in the United States that engage meaningfully with targeted audiences to build trust and mutual understanding. On the other hand, it aims to provide a framework for rapid action as well as enhancing opportunities for engagement when they arise through a Policy Dialogue Support Facility mechanism. The action enables sustained engagement with decision makers, media and opinion shapers, civil society, business and industry leaders, think tanks, academia, youth, and the cultural and creative sectors. By using a combination of policy dialogue support and public diplomacy, the action will enhance the visibility and credibility of the EU in the USA and contribute to closer alignment between EU and U.S. policy positions and approaches, including on major foreign policy, security, economic, digital and global governance challenges. The action will target federal, State and local level stakeholders on key priority areas based on mutual interest and ability to develop cooperation.

description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), MH-60 PMA-299 (AIR � 2.3.4.2), Patuxent River, MD intends to negotiate multiple sole-source orders over a five-period (FY27-FY31) under Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N00019-26-G-1012 with Thales Defense & Security, Inc. (TDSI), 22605 Gateway Center Dr Clarksburg, MD 20871, to support product support, development, sustaining engineering, repairs, spares, and logistical services associated with the AN/AQS-22 Airborne Low Frequency Sonar (ALFS) system for integration into MH-60R, Multi-Mission Helicopter. This notice also publicizes the government�s intent to negotiate and award the first planned task order under this BOA. This initial order will require a Sustaining Engineering evaluation for three (3) separate Government Furnished Equipment (GFE) Specialized Test Equipment (STE) benches. The Government intends to negotiate the initial and all subsequent BOA orders with TDSI under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. This notice is published to identify interested responsible sources and obtain information regarding their capability to meet the stated requirement. The Government will consider timely submissions in determining whether a source is capable of meeting the requirement to satisfy FAR Part 10 and DFARS206.103-170. This notice also serves as the pre-solicitation synopsis requirements of FAR Part 5 for the initial task order. Future orders under the BOA will be synopsized individually as they arise. issued 2.0 REQUIREMENT DESCRIPTION 2.1 Overarching BOA Scope The anticipated orders issued under BOA N000926G1012 will encompass product support, Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE), development, and sustaining engineering supplies and services required to support the MH-60R Mission System AN/AQS-22 Airborne Low Frequency Sonar (ALFS) Weapon Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs). The primary WRAs include: Transducer Assembly (TA) Reeling Machine (RM) Reeling Machine Interface Unit (RMIU) Reeling Machine Control Unit (RMCU) Reel and Cable (R&C) The five-year scope includes NRE, recurring services, material, component repair, and logistical support to sustain and mitigate obsolescence across both active and delivered systems for the U.S. Navy and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) customers. 2.2 First Planned Task Order Scope The initial order to be executed under the BOA requires a Sustaining Engineering evaluation for the three (3) specific GFE STE benches associated with the AN/AQS-22 ALFS program: Reeling Machine Test Bench (RMTB) Transducer Assembly Test Bench (TATB) Reeling Machine Control System Test Bench (RMCSTB) This effort comprises engineering evaluations, hardware/software analysis, and documentation support to establish the test bench baseline configuration and Technical Data Package (TDP) for each bench., 3.0 SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION This acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." TDSI is the U.S. based subsidiary of Thales Underwater Systems SAS (TUS), the original designer, developer, and manufacturer of the AN/AQS-22 ALFS System Weapon Replaceable Assemblies (WRAs) for the Transducer Assembly (TA), Reeling Machine (RM), Reeling Machine Interface Unit (RMIU), Reeling Machine Control Unit (RMCU) and Reel and Cable (R&C). TUS owns the proprietary data for these WRAs that is required to perform the efforts herein, including the applicable specifications, source code, and drawings. Thus, TDSI has access and rights to the proprietary drawings and data required to perform these efforts efficiently and effectively. TDSI is also the current repair facility for TAs and the only source with domestic facilities, data, and experience to complete these efforts. No other firm possesses the required knowledge, experience, expertise, and proprietary technical and software data packages required to successfully fulfill this order in a timely and cost-effective manner. 4.0 SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS (CAPABILITY STATEMENT) Responsible sources may submit a capability statement, which will be considered by the agency. The capability statement must include your approach to accomplish this effort in support of the H-60 Helicopter Program. title: Graphite Furnace Atomic Absorption Spectrometer
description: Sources Sought Notice for Graphite Furnace Atomic Absorption Spectrometer Notice ID: NIST-MML-FY27-SS01 Response Date: 11/28/2026 Product Service Code (PSC): 6640 NAICS Code: 334516 Background The Inorganic Chemical Metrology Group (ICMG) uses at least two measurement methods, each based on orthogonal physical principles, to certify the trace elements in candidate standard reference materials (SRM). These SRMs are intended for method validation and quality assurance in trace-element measurements to assess the nutritional value and contaminant status of agricultural products. A sensitive trace-element detector, a graphite furnace atomic absorption spectrometer (GFAAS) is sought to complement the group's inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometric (ICP-MS) measurement capability and fulfill the two independent method requirements for SRM development. Consideration will be given to GFAAS capable of direct solid-sample analysis to maximize its orthogonality relative to the liquid-sampling-based ICP-MS technique. title: Request for Information (RFI) for Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological and Nuclear Protection (JPM CBRN P) Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS)
description: This is a request for information (RFI) only for capabilities and experience which show potential for meeting the requirements described below. This is not a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Request for Proposal (RFP) or an Invitation for Bid (IFB). It is a market research tool being used to determine the availability and adequacy of potential sources for planning purposes only. Responses to this notice are not considered as offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of responses nor otherwise pay for the preparation of any information presented or the use of any such information. 1. Purpose The Joint Project Manager for Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Protection (JPM CBRN P) is conducting a market survey to identify industry capabilities, experience, and potential approaches for serving as a Product Support Integrator (PSI) and material integration support for the Chemically Protected Deployable Medical System (CP DEPMEDS) Reconfiguration and Technology Refresh effort. The Government seeks a commercial partner capable of procuring and coordinating the delivery of commercially available components; receiving, tracking, and consolidating Government-sourced components; applying Item Unique Identification (IUID) markings as required; maintaining materiel accountability and readiness; conducting Preventative Maintenance, Checks and Services (PMCS) and Care of Supply in Storage (COSIS) as necessary, and delivering verified, complete component packages to Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA) for final system integration, build completion, and packaging. This RFI is issued solely for planning and market-research purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, request for proposal, commitment by the Government, or authorization to incur costs. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. 2. Background CP DEPMEDS is a fielded CBRN protection system that supports Army Role 3 field-hospital operations. The program is executing a reconfiguration and technology-refresh effort using fielded, previously qualified, and commercially available components. The revised support concept under consideration would use a commercial PSI to integrate component procurement, Government-furnished or Government-sourced materiel coordination, traceability, IUID marking, and delivery to Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA). PBA would retain responsibility for final assembly/integration of CP DEPMEDS sets, final packaging, associated Government acceptance activities, and delivery of sets to their fielding/final destination. 3. Scope of Information Requested The Government seeks information on industry capability to perform the following functions: A. Commercial Component Procurement Procure commercially available components identified by the Government. Conduct vendor management and order placement of components. Identify long-lead items, supply-chain constraints, discontinuance risks, and proposed alternate sources. Provide proposed substitutes only when specifically authorized by the Government. Manage warranties, vendor documentation, certificates of conformance, and commercial shipping documentation as applicable. B. Government Component Coordination Coordinate receipt, transfer, and consolidation of Government-sourced components from designated Government organizations, depots, supply activities, or other locations. Maintain accountability for Government-provided or Government-directed materiel while in contractor custody. Maintain COSIS to prevent environmental degradation, corrosion, and shelf life expiration of stored equipment and supplies. Reconcile shipping discrepancies, damaged materiel, shortages, overages, and documentation issues. Maintain traceability between each component, its source, and its assigned CP DEPMEDS configuration or set. Note: The contractor would not independently obligate Government funds or direct Government supply activities. The Government would retain authority for requisitions, funding, release, acceptance, and disposition decisions. C. IUID and Asset Identification Apply, validate, and document IUID markings for designated end items and components in accordance with Government-furnished requirements and applicable standards. Verify marking quality, placement, readability, and association with the correct item record. Maintain item-level records linking serial number, part number, National Stock Number, Unique Item Identifier, source, and destination. Provide electronic IUID and asset-accountability data deliverables in a Government-specified format. D. Materiel Receiving, Inspection, and Staging Receive and inspect commercial and Government-sourced components. Verify quantities, part numbers, serial numbers, condition, shelf life, and required documentation. Store and stage components in a manner that preserves condition, supports shelf-life management, and enables rapid consolidation into required delivery packages. Maintain COSIS to prevent environmental degradation, corrosion, and shelf life expiration of stored equipment and supplies. E. Kit Completion and Delivery to PBA Build component-level shipping packages in accordance with Government-approved bills of material, configuration lists, and delivery priorities. Conduct kit-completeness checks before shipment. Package, preserve, mark, and ship components to PBA in accordance with Government-approved shipping instructions. Provide advance-shipment notifications, packing lists, serial-number/IUID records, and discrepancy reports. If required, travel to PBA to help support the delivery and inventory of shipped equipment. F. Program Management and Reporting Maintain an integrated procurement and delivery schedule. Provide recurring status reports addressing procurement status, component availability, shortages, long-lead risks, delivery forecasts, IUID status, kit completion, and shipment status. Identify risks early and recommend mitigation actions, including alternate vendors, phased deliveries, or proposed substitutes. Participate in Government-led integrated product team meetings as required. 4. Desired Capabilities Respondents should describe experience performing comparable work involving: Multi-vendor procurement and materiel integration; Government-furnished property or Government-directed materiel; IUID marking, validation, and data management; Military logistics, asset accountability, and shipping documentation; Kitting, staging, packaging, preservation, and shipment of complex equipment; Supply-chain risk management and long-lead-item mitigation; CBRN, deployable medical, field-hospital, shelter, or comparable expeditionary equipment. (Note: This is desired experience but not required for response.) The Government is particularly interested in respondents able to manage multiple sources of supply and coordinate delivery of components to a Government integration location. 5. Industry Response Instructions Responses should not exceed [15] pages, excluding attachments. Include: Company Information: Name, UEI, CAGE code, business size, socioeconomic status, and points of contact. Relevant Experience: Up to three relevant efforts performed within the past five years. Technical Approach: Notional approach to commercial procurement, Government-component coordination, IUID, accountability, staging, kit verification, and delivery to PBA. Facilities and Workforce: Relevant facilities, quality systems, logistics staff, IUID capability, and geographic support model. Data and Reporting: Proposed methods for inventory visibility, serialized-item traceability, IUID data delivery, and Government status reporting. Risk Management: Principal risks, including vendor lead time, part obsolescence, Government materiel availability, configuration changes, and transportation delays. Udbuddet omfatter vask og leje af tekstiler inden for det sundhedsfaglige område til både Tårnby Kommune og Dragør Kommune og består af følgende to delaftaler: • Delaftale 1: Vask og leje af arbejdsbeklædning • Delaftale 2: Vask og leje af linned Tilbudsgiver kan vælge at afgive tilbud på en eller begge delaftaler. Et tilbud på en delaftale skal omfatte det samlede udbudte forbrug under den pågældende delaftale for både Tårnby Kommune og Dragør Kommune. Det er således ikke muligt at afgive tilbud alene på en af kommunernes forbrug inden for en delaftale. Delaftalerne evalueres og tildeles særskilt. Den enkelte delaftale tildeles den tilbudsgiver, der har afgivet det økonomisk mest fordelagtige tilbud på den pågældende delaftale i overensstemmelse med den evalueringsmodel, der fremgår af udbudsmaterialet. Den samme tilbudsgiver kan således tildeles en eller begge delaftaler. Tilbud, der ikke omfatter begge kommuners samlede udbudte forbrug inden for den eller de delaftaler, som tilbudsgiver afgiver tilbud på, vil blive betragtet som ukonditionsmæssigt. På baggrund af tildelingen underskrives kontrakten særskilt for hver kommune. Der vil således blive indgået en kontrakt mellem den vindende tilbudsgiver og Tårnby Kommune og en kontrakt mellem den vindende tilbudsgiver og Dragør Kommune for hver delaftale, som tilbudsgiveren tildeles. Kontrakterne har som udgangspunkt samme ordlyd og indeholder de samme vilkår. Der kan dog være forskelle i bestemmelserne om kommunernes arbejdsklausuler, som er tilpasset den enkelte kommune. De delaftalespecifikke krav fremgår af kontrakternes respektive bilag. Udbudsbetingelserne med tilhørende bilag udgør sammen med den enkelte kontrakt det samlede kontraktgrundlag. Udbuddet gennemføres via EU-Supply, hvor det samlede udbudsmateriale er offentligt tilgængeligt. Ved behov for support eller systemtekniske spørgsmål i forbindelse med udbuddet henvises til EU-Supply på e-mail dksupport@eu-supply.com eller telefon +45 7020 8014.

title: JOFOC-Clinical East Staffing
description: The Government proposes a noncompetitive modification to Task Order 75P00123F37008, issued under Contract HHSP233201800009I, to provide interim bridge services while FOH completes the competitive follow-on acquisition and transition. The proposed modification would establish a six-month base period, November 1, 2026 through April 30, 2027, and one six-month option, May 1 through October 31, 2027. The proposed modification will increase the total estimated cost of the task order by $19,978,602.20, from $62,094,434.91 to $82,073,037.11. Performance will be limited to the services and duration supported by the approved justification and implemented through the executed modification. Task Order 75P00123F37008 (Clinical East), issued under IDIQ Contract HHSP233201800009I, is a time and-materials (T&M) task order with ServeFed, Inc. Before execution of the proposed modification, the Contracting Officer will confirm the applicable contract-type requirements, review the availability of any existing determination and findings (D&F), and document the basis for continued use of T&M or any proposed change in contract type. The proposed modification is necessary to maintain uninterrupted mission-essential services while the Government completes and awards the competitive follow-on acquisition. The recompete is currently under development but will not be completed before expiration of the existing contract on October 31, 2026. The Government anticipates award of the bridge modification in October 2026, using FY 2027 Service Supply funds, subject to availability and proper obligation of funds. The proposed bridge period is November 1, 2026 through October 31, 2027. The Government intends to transition to the competitively awarded follow-on contract as soon as practicable and does not intend to use the entire bridge period if transition to the successor contractor can occur earlier. The Government plans to solicit for the recompete in FY27.
